CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess the management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, with a focus on recent symptom changes and medication efficacy.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his scheduled follow-up appointment, reporting a mixed response to his current treatment regimen. He states that while his anxiety levels have remained stable, he has experienced an uptick in the frequency of his tension-type headaches, now occurring approximately 3 times per week, with a moderate intensity rating of 5 out of 10. Mr. Smith attributes this increase to heightened work stress and prolonged hours on the computer, which he believes may be contributing to his headache patterns.
Sleep quality has deteriorated slightly; Mr. Smith reports averaging only 6 hours of sleep per night with increased episodes of waking during the night. He continues to take trazodone and melatonin but finds that these may not be as effective as previously. Despite this, he remains committed to his yoga practice and has added guided meditation sessions to his routine, which he finds somewhat helpful.
Mr. Smith expresses ongoing concerns regarding his persistent fatigue, which he describes as more pronounced in the mornings and lessening as the day progresses. He is unsure if this is related to his sleep disturbances or work-related stress. He has also experienced mild dizziness on occasion, which he describes as infrequent and not debilitating.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 250 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime (review for efficacy) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime (review for efficacy) 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 50 mg daily (consider increasing dosage) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, reporting that his workload has increased recently, leading to additional stress. He remains physically active, participating in running groups and attending yoga classes. He adheres to a healthy diet, abstaining from alcohol and limiting caffeine intake.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels stable; sleep quality decreased; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Increased headache frequency; mild dizziness; no visual disturbances or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue continues, with no fever or weight changes noted.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, appears slightly fatigued; mood appears stable but with mild anxiety noted. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; mild dizziness reported. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with no signs of distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 250 mg daily. Monitor for any changes in anxiety levels. Consider increasing lorazepam to 1 mg twice a week for acute episodes if needed. 2. Insomnia: Review the efficacy of trazodone and melatonin. If sleep disturbances persist, consider adjusting the dosage or exploring alternative sleep aids. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Increase topiramate dosage to 100 mg daily, as the patient reports increased frequency and intensity. Continue amitriptyline at 50 mg nightly. Schedule a follow-up in one month to assess response to the medication change. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Evaluate the potential impact of sleep quality on fatigue levels. If symptoms persist, consider a referral to a sleep specialist for further evaluation. Encourage continued engagement in physical activity and mindfulness practices.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-04-01 to monitor symptom changes, evaluate treatment efficacy, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
